messages:
jess: Hey team — AcmeCorp is seeing truncated streaming responses from the SSE endpoint. The stream just stops and the final JSON object (and finish_reason) never arrives. Happens ~30% of streams, more often from mobile clients behind Akamai. Request ID: req_0a9f7e2c. Model: redwood-v1-large.

lena: Thanks — can you paste a minimal curl repro and whether they're using HTTP/2 or any CDN/proxy in front? Also: are they rotating auth tokens mid-stream? :thinking_face:

jess: Repro (customer):
```
curl -N -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-large","input":"summarize this...","stream":true}'
```
They report HTTP/2 from mobile -> Akamai -> our edge. No auth rotation per their report (single short-lived token used).

raj: Hypothesis: edge/proxy is cutting connection early (idle timeout or buffering) or client SDK is triggering a reconnect that drops final chunk. Can you ask them to run curl directly from a host bypassing Akamai? Also check Akamai (or Fastly) keepalive/idle timeout configs.

taylor: We saw a similar pattern where the client SDK would refresh the Authorization header in-memory and issue a new request, which caused racey reconnects. But that started happening >20s in for us — your 8–12s window suggests a proxy timeout.

jess: I asked them to try direct curl from a GCE VM (no CDN). They got the full stream there consistently. So that points to Akamai/config.

lena: Can you ask them to capture a verbose curl (-v) or tcpdump showing a TCP FIN/RST at the moment of truncation and post the headers? Also ask if there is any intermediate device rewriting connection headers (Proxy-Connection, Connection: keep-alive).

jess: Asked. They posted this excerpt (sanitized):
```
*client* <- *edge*: FIN, then no more data.
server response headers included: Server: AkamaiGHost, Connection: keep-alive, Transfer-Encoding: chunked
```
They also see incomplete SSE data like: `data: {"id":"resp_xxx","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"..."}}` then stream ends (no closing braces, no finish_reason).

raj: That matches a proxy-level hard close. Two actionable items: 1) Ask Akamai to increase idle timeout or disable http/2 graceful shutdown for SSE paths. 2) We can add periodic heartbeat SSE events (server side) to keep the connection busy; I can whip up a flag to emit "event: heartbeat" every 5s for streams from certain customers.

taylor: Short-term client workaround: make the SDK tolerate truncated final SSE and attempt resume by calling the API with the last token id or last partial output (we can add support for a resume header: `X-Resume-Last-Event: <last_event_id>`). If the server still has cached KV prefix, it can continue. But that's a product change.

lena: For now, ask the customer to disable any Akamai "early close" rules and to whitelist api.redwood.ai for streaming. Also ask them to test with `--no-buffer` and with keepalive headers explicitly set.

jess: Will relay. They also asked if the absence of `finish_reason` in the final choice is expected — we should surface a clear error when stream cuts final frame.

raj: Agreed — we should log an alert when a stream connection is closed without emitting a terminal frame. I'll add a quick SLO check to the stream router metrics and an internal alert to catch sudden spikes.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: stream-heartbeat-proposal -> canary (eng-runtime). ETA 30m.

lena: Thanks all. I'll keep the thread open until we get Akamai confirmation or we ship the heartbeat canary. :thumbsup:
